meaning:
δια-λογισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(διαλογίζομαι) [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲשָׁבָה ;]
a thought, reasoning, inward questioning: Mat.15:19, Mrk.7:21, Luk.2:35 5:22 6:8 9:46, 47 24:38, Rom.1:21 14:1, 1Co.3:20" (LXX), Php.2:14; κριταὶ δ. πονηρῶν, genitive of qual. (cf. Pro.12:5), Jas.2:4; χωρὶς ὀργῆς καὶ δ. (where perh. δ., like מְזִמָּה, in Ps 138(139):20, al., implies evil intention), 1Ti.2:8 (see Hort, in l.; cf. Cremer, 400).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.
For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,
Yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
Because knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, and didn’t give thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened.
And again, “The Lord knows the reasoning of the wise, that it is worthless.”
Do all things without complaining and arguing,
I desire therefore that the men in every place pray, lifting up holy hands without anger and doubting.
haven’t you shown partiality among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?
